newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Koncar mulls new strategy ahead of float.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Koncar mulls new strategy ahead of float.

text.p: Croatia's largest electrical company Koncar d.d. said on Friday it was still mulling a new business strategy to prepare the way for a flotation in about a year's time.
"We are in a very early phase and actual preparations can begin only after financial consolidation," Ivan Cesarec, assistant to the chief executive, told Reuters by telephone.
Addressing an investment conference earlier today, Privatisation Minister Ivan Penic said Koncar would be the next leading Croatian company, after drugs firm Pliva, to be listed on foreign bourses.
Pliva was first privatised last March through a global share offering and Cesarec said Koncar would probably do the same.
Koncar's supervisory board has just devised new development plans to the year 2000, which envisage listing it on both the Zagreb and London Stock Exchanges.
But there are no plans yet to offer to investors a specific portion of its 365 million marks equity, of which the government still controls over 60 percent, Cesarec said.
First of all, he said radical cuts in loss-making parts of business and sizeable investments to improve the company's market position would be needed to boost its profitability.
It also still had to have its accounts submitted for review by independent foreign auditors.
"All this may take until the end of September next year," Cesarec said but made clear Koncar was in no hurry which may reduce the success of its flotation.
"To list our shares now would be foolish, they would not quote very high. But they will be worth a lot more after restructuring." -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
